template_name: Consent Order / Tomlin Schedule Enforcement Review
description: Evaluates whether a party has breached the terms of a consent order or Tomlin schedule and whether the court should enter judgment or grant enforcement remedies.
application_scenario: Applications to enter judgment or enforce terms after a party defaults on a court-sanctioned settlement agreement in property or trespass disputes.
reasoning_flow: Review the terms of the consent order or the schedule to the Tomlin Order.
Determine whether the defaulting party has failed to perform their specified obligations within the agreed timeframe.
Assess any reasons or defenses raised by the defaulting party (e.g., breakdown in representation, financial difficulty).
Evaluate whether the terms of the settlement are clear, precise, and legally enforceable.
Enter judgment or grant specific enforcement orders in accordance with the terms of the consent framework.
example_application: In a trespass and adverse possession dispute, the parties enter into a Tomlin Order to resolve boundary issues. The defendant fails to remove illegal structures as scheduled. The plaintiff applies to the court to enforce the Tomlin Order and enter judgment.

description: Evaluates whether an occupier of land has established both physical possession and the requisite intention to exclude the world, including the paper owner, for the statutory limitation period.
application_scenario: Where an occupier claims possessory title to land and defends against an action for possession or seeks a declaration of ownership.
reasoning_flow: Determine the relevant statutory limitation period for bringing an action to recover land under local limitation statutes.
Assess whether the occupier had exclusive physical control over the disputed land, examining structural features such as fencing, locks, and utility accounts.
Evaluate whether the occupier possessed the subjective and objective intent to exclude the world at large, including the paper owner (animus possidendi).
Verify if the possession was continuous, uninterrupted, and without the owner's consent or written acknowledgment of title.
Conclude whether the paper owner's title is extinguished and if the occupier has acquired possessory title.
example_application: An occupier of a plot of land who has lived there, run a business, and maintained exclusive control using fences and locked gates since the late 1990s defends against a registered owner's claim for possession by asserting adverse possession.

template_name: Requisition on Title & Root of Title Verification
description: Determines whether a purchaser's requisition on property title was raised within contractually specified time limits, or if it goes to the 'root of title,' thereby exempting it from such limits.
application_scenario: Disputes where a purchaser refuses to complete a transaction due to an unresolved title defect, and the vendor claims the requisition was raised too late.
reasoning_flow: Identify the contractual timeline stipulated for raising requisitions on title.
Examine the specific nature of the title requisition raised by the purchaser (such as unauthorized structural alterations or missing original deeds).
Analyze whether the defect constitutes a challenge to the 'root of title' (i.e., whether the vendor lacks the legal power to pass the interest agreed upon).
If the requisition goes to the root of title, hold that the contractual time bar does not apply to it.
Determine if the vendor has successfully answered or discharged the burden of showing good title.
example_application: In a property transaction, the purchaser discovers a major unauthorized building alteration that could trigger government re-entry. Although raised past the contractual 14-day limit, the court holds it goes to the root of title, making the time limit inapplicable.

template_name: Summary Judgment Triable Issue Test (Property Disputes)
description: Assesses whether a defendant in a property or conveyancing dispute has raised an arguable defense or triable issue sufficient to defeat a summary judgment application.
application_scenario: Application by a plaintiff for summary judgment under civil procedure rules regarding property possession, breach of sale agreement, or return of deposit.
reasoning_flow: Verify whether the plaintiff has made out a prima facie case of entitlement (e.g., registered ownership, clear contractual breach).
Examine the defendant's affidavit or defense to identify assertions of law or fact (such as oral variations, estoppel, or waiver).
Determine if the asserted defense is bona fide and has a real prospect of success, as opposed to being sham or shadowy.
Assess whether the resolution of the dispute requires a full trial with oral testimony and cross-examination.
Grant or deny summary leave to defend based on the existence of a triable issue.
example_application: A buyer seeks summary judgment for the return of a deposit after the vendor fails to show good title. The vendor asserts there was an oral agreement to extend the completion date, creating a triable issue of fact requiring a full trial.

description: Balances a landlord's claim for possession of domestic premises for personal use against the statutory protections and hardship of the tenant.
application_scenario: Actions for recovery of domestic premises under statutory landlord-tenant regimes where the landlord claims a residential need for self or immediate family.
reasoning_flow: Verify that the landlord has a bona fide and reasonable requirement to occupy the premises as a residence.
Evaluate the landlord's current living conditions, family size, and alternative accommodations available.
Assess the tenant's circumstances, including duration of tenancy, family income, physical health, and alternative housing options.
Perform a comparative hardship analysis to determine which party would suffer greater distress or prejudice if possession were granted or refused.
Determine whether it is just and equitable under all circumstances to issue an order for possession.
example_application: A retired owner of a flat seeks possession of their leased unit to live with their aging parents. The tenant, who has lived there for a decade and has limited financial means, resists on grounds of severe hardship.

template_name: Partition Ordinance Compulsory Sale and Partition Evaluation
description: Analyzes whether co-owned land or property that cannot be physically partitioned should be ordered for sale under statutory partition frameworks.
application_scenario: An application by a co-owner or a chargee of a co-owner's share for an order for sale of the entire property under the Partition Ordinance.
reasoning_flow: Confirm the applicant's locus standi (such as a registered co-owner or a legal chargee of an undivided share).
Determine whether the property is physically or practically capable of partition without causing significant loss of value.
If partition is impracticable, evaluate whether an order for sale would be beneficial to all parties or if any party has raised compelling reasons against it.
Assess the valuation of the property and determine the fair distribution of the sale proceeds.
Formulate appropriate terms for the sale, such as giving the parties a set timeframe to sell the property privately before a public auction.
example_application: A money lender holding a charge over an undivided share of a residential flat applies for an order of sale under the Partition Ordinance because the property is physically indivisible and the loan remains unpaid.

template_name: Mesne Profits and Holding Over Damages Valuation
description: Calculates the quantum of damages or mesne profits payable by a tenant or occupier who unlawfully holds over after the termination or expiry of a tenancy.
application_scenario: An assessment of damages proceeding following a judgment for possession against a tenant who failed to deliver vacant possession.
reasoning_flow: Identify the exact period of the unlawful holding over or trespass.
Determine whether mesne profits should be calculated based on the contractually agreed rent, the prevailing market rent, or effective rent (discounting temporal fluctuations).
Evaluate expert valuation evidence of comparable properties in the immediate vicinity during the relevant holding over period.
Adjust calculations for factors such as occupancy rates, bulk discounts, or licensing/operating expenses where appropriate.
Calculate the total sum due, including any contractual rates, management fees, or government rent.
example_application: A commercial tenant fails to reinstate and vacate a warehouse for two months after lease expiration. The court assesses mesne profits using the effective market rent and adjusts for the reasonable time required for actual reinstatement.

template_name: Deed of Mutual Covenant (DMC) Enforcement & Mandatory Injunction Test
description: Evaluates whether an owner's alteration or structure breaches the Deed of Mutual Covenant (DMC) and warrants the equitable remedy of a mandatory injunction.
application_scenario: An application by a building manager or incorporated owners to compel an owner to remove unauthorized structures, signs, or modifications.
reasoning_flow: Interpret the relevant restrictive covenants of the DMC (e.g., bans on external alterations, common area obstructions, or unauthorized signage).
Determine whether the disputed structure or alteration physically violates these covenants.
Evaluate any defenses raised by the owner, such as express permission, waiver, estoppel, or long-standing acquiescence by the management.
Assess whether the manager or incorporated owners took prompt and reasonable action once they became aware of the breach.
Balance the equities, considering hardship and the public interest in maintaining building safety, to decide if a mandatory injunction is the appropriate remedy.
example_application: The incorporated owners of an industrial building seek a mandatory injunction to force a tenant to remove large illuminated signs erected on the outer wall, which the tenant claims had been tolerated for several years under an informal agreement.

template_name: Land Registry Entry Vacation (Good Cause & Validity Check)
description: Evaluates applications to vacate a registered encumbrance, lis pendens, or assent from the Land Registry on grounds of invalidity or lack of bona fide prosecution.
application_scenario: Applications under land registration legislation to clear title of registered entries that impede sale or transfer.
reasoning_flow: Examine the legal nature of the registered entry (such as lis pendens, assent, or prohibitory order).
Verify if the underlying legal action or instrument is valid (e.g., checking if a transfer assent violated statutory alienation restrictions without prior consent, making it void).
Determine if the entry has expired or if the corresponding litigation is being prosecuted in good faith and with reasonable speed.
If the entry is found to be void or the claim is not prosecuted bona fide, establish that the registration lacks legal effect on the land.
Order the registrar to vacate and discharge the entry to restore the marketable title.
example_application: An administrator of an estate seeks to vacate a registered assent on a property because the transfer was executed under a statutory scheme without mandatory prior approval from the housing authority, rendering the assent legally void.

template_name: Variation of Costs Order Nisi (Parties' Conduct & Outcome Balance)
description: Determines whether the standard rule that 'costs follow the event' should be departed from or varied due to the unreasonable conduct of the parties or partial success.
application_scenario: Inter partes application to vary a costs order nisi after the delivery of a judgment.
reasoning_flow: Identify the 'successful party' or the general 'event' of the litigation.
Assess whether either party raised unreasonable, scandalous, or completely failed issues that significantly prolonged the trial or increased costs.
Evaluate the effect of any settlement offers, such as Calderbank letters or sanctioned offers, and whether they were beaten or unreasonably rejected.
Consider whether the parties acted cooperatively or lititgiously throughout the dispute.
Determine if an alternative costs order (such as no order as to costs, percentage reduction, or indemnity costs) is justified in the interest of justice.
example_application: After a complex trial regarding a tenancy dispute, the plaintiff wins a minor return of deposit but fails on all major claims of breach of contract. The defendant successfully applies to vary the costs order nisi so that the plaintiff pays the bulk of the litigation costs.

description: Distinguishes whether an occupancy agreement creates a contractual licence (revocable at will) or a tenancy (granting estate interest and statutory protection).
application_scenario: Disputes where a landowner seeks immediate eviction of an occupier, and the occupier claims a tenancy status that triggers statutory protection or notice periods.
reasoning_flow: Analyze the terms of the written or oral agreement between the landowner and the occupier.
Determine whether the occupier was granted exclusive possession of the defined area.
Evaluate whether the payment terms, duration, and parties' conduct indicate an intention to create an estate in land (tenancy) or merely a personal privilege (licence).
Assess if any implied conditions or extrinsic factors (such as management rules) negate exclusive control.
Conclude the legal status of the occupancy and apply the corresponding statutory notice or termination requirements.
example_application: An owner of a parking space revokes a user's right to park due to alleged violations of parking rules. The user argues that the parking arrangement is a tenancy and requires proper statutory notice to quit, while the owner contends it is a mere licence at will.

description: Verifies whether an applicant has satisfied the statutory conditions (ownership percentage, age/repair status, and fair negotiations) for the compulsory sale of land for redevelopment.
application_scenario: Land tribunal proceedings where a majority owner applies to compel the sale of remaining undivided shares in a building.
reasoning_flow: Verify that the applicant owns the requisite statutory minimum percentage of undivided shares in the lot (such as 80% or 90%).
Evaluate expert evidence concerning the age and physical state of repair of the existing building to determine if redevelopment is justified.
Determine if the costs of repair and maintenance of the existing building are disproportionate to its remaining economic value.
Assess whether the applicant has taken reasonable steps to negotiate for the purchase of all undivided shares on fair and reasonable terms.
Conclude whether to grant the order for compulsory sale and set the reserve price.
example_application: A property developer holding 92% of the undivided shares of a 60-year-old building applies for a compulsory sale order, submitting structural surveys demonstrating severe concrete spalling and uneconomical repair costs.

template_name: Relief Against Forfeiture vs. Liquidated Damages
description: Analyzes whether a vendor's forfeiture of a deposit or a contract clause claiming outstanding balances operates as an unenforceable penalty or a valid liquidated damages provision.
application_scenario: Disputes arising from aborted sales agreements where the purchaser defaults and seeks the return of payments made, claiming they are penalties.
reasoning_flow: Identify the default provisions in the contract (e.g., forfeiture of deposit, payment of outstanding balance upon breach).
Determine whether the deposit percentage is in line with customary market standards (e.g., 10%) or is excessive.
Evaluate whether the clause imposing further financial liabilities is a genuine pre-estimate of loss or is designed in terrorem to coerce performance (a penalty).
Examine whether the innocent party suffered actual losses and if they took reasonable steps to mitigate those losses (e.g., timely resale).
Order the return of the sum if it is a penalty, or allow forfeiture if it represents a standard deposit or reasonable liquidated damages.
example_application: A purchaser fails to complete a land sale. The vendor forfeits the 10% deposit and seeks further damages based on a contract clause. The court reviews if the additional damages claim constitutes an invalid penalty or is a standard compensatory mechanism.

template_name: Restitution and Unjust Enrichment in Property Transactions
description: Determines whether a party is entitled to restitution for benefits conferred or payments made under a property agreement that was subsequently aborted or found void.
application_scenario: Claims for the return of deposits, pre-payments, or expenses incurred in anticipation of a lease or sale of property that fell through.
reasoning_flow: Establish whether the defendant received a benefit (such as money paid as a deposit, pre-payment, or improvements made to land) at the plaintiff's expense.
Determine if the transfer of benefit was based on a contract or agreement that has been terminated, rescinded, or is void ab initio.
Assess whether there is any legal or contractual basis (such as a forfeiture clause) allowing the defendant to retain the benefit.
Analyze if retaining the benefit would be unjust under the circumstances (e.g., total failure of consideration).
Order restitution of the benefit to the plaintiff, subject to any valid counterclaims or set-offs.
example_application: A company pays a substantial non-refundable prepayment to secure a licensing lease. The agreement is terminated before performance begins. The court evaluates whether the company is entitled to a refund of the prepayment under principles of unjust enrichment and failed consideration.
